academic_translation: That place will become worthy of being bowed to and worthy of being circumambulated,
translation: That place will become worthy of being bowed to and walked around,

academic_translation: that place will become like a stūpa.
translation: and that place will become like a shrine.

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up, retain, keep, read, and master these words of such a sūtra will be tormented,

locked_terms.use: son or daughter of a good family

translation: Also, Subhuti, any son or daughter of a good family who takes up, remembers, keeps, reads, and masters the words of such a sacred text will be tormented,

academic_translation: they will be severely tormented.
translation: They will suffer greatly.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, because those sentient beings are tormented in this very life for whatever non-virtuous actions they committed in previous lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms, those non-virtuous actions they committed in previous lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms will be purified,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, these living beings suffer in this very life for bad actions they did in past lives. Those bad actions would lead to an unhappy rebirth. Because they suffer now, those bad actions from past lives that lead to an unhappy rebirth will be washed away.

academic_translation: and they will also attain the awakening of a Buddha.
translation: And they will also reach the awakening of a Buddha.

academic_translation: Subhūti, I remember that in the past, measureless and even more than measureless eons ago, before and even further before the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara, eighty-four hundred thousand million myriad Buddhas appeared, whom I pleased,
translation: Subhuti, I remember the past, countless and more than countless long ages ago. It was before, even long before, the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha Dipankara. Back then, eighty-four million billion Buddhas appeared. I made them happy.

academic_translation: and having not displeased them, did not disappoint them.
translation: I did not upset them, and I did not let them down.

tibetan: རབ་འབྱོར་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་དག་ངས་མཉེས་པར་བྱས་ནས་ཐུགས་འབྱུང་བར་མ་བྱས་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང༌། ཕྱི་མའི་དུས་ལྔ་བརྒྱའི་ཐ་མར་གྱུར་པ་ན། མདོ་སྡེ་འདི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། འདྲི་བ་དང༌། འཛིན་པ་དང་འཆང་བ་དང༌། ཀློག་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་ལས། རབ་འབྱོར་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སྔ་མས་བརྒྱའི་ཆར་ཡང་ཉེ་བར་མི་འགྲོ།
academic_translation: Subhūti, regarding whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, and whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, upholds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
translation: Subhuti, think of how I made those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, happy and did not let them down. Now imagine someone else when the last five hundred years have come. This person takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, and fully understands this sacred text. Subhuti, compared to this person's pile of stored-up goodness, my old pile of stored-up goodness is not even one hundredth as big.

academic_translation: It does not bear comparison to a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, a number, a measure, a calculation, an analogy, a match, or even a cause.
translation: It cannot be compared to a thousandth part or a hundred-thousandth part. It cannot be compared to any number, measure, counting, example, match, or even a cause.

academic_translation: Subhūti, if I were to describe the mass of merit of those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family, however great a mass of merit those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family would fully uphold at that time, sentient beings would go mad and their minds would be confounded.

locked_terms.use: son of a good family or daughter of a good family

translation: Subhuti, what if I described the pile of stored-up goodness of those sons of a good family or daughters of a good family? If I told them how great a pile of stored-up goodness those sons of a good family or daughters of a good family would hold at that time, living beings would go mad. Their minds would be completely confused.

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, this Dharma discourse is inconceivable,
translation: Also, Subhuti, this lesson on the teaching cannot be imagined.

academic_translation: and its ripening should also be known to be simply inconceivable.
translation: And you should know that its ripening cannot be imagined either.

academic_translation: Then the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One thus:
translation: Then the honored Subhuti said this to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
translation: "Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the awakening hero's vehicle live?"

academic_translation: How should they practice?
translation: How should they practice?

academic_translation: How should the mind be fully held?
translation: How should they fully hold the mind?

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
translation: When he had said this, the Blessed One spoke to honored Subhuti:

academic_translation: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I shall lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.'

locked_terms.use: freedom from sorrow with no group left over

translation: Subhuti, anyone who has correctly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should think like this: 'I will lead all living beings to complete freedom from sorrow in the expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over.'

academic_translation: Even though immeasurable sentient beings have been led to complete nirvāṇa in this way, they should generate the mind thinking, 'No sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.'
translation: Even though countless living beings are led to complete freedom from sorrow in this way, they should set the mind to think: 'Not a single living being has been led to complete freedom from sorrow.'

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, they are not to be called a bodhisattva;
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, if an awakening hero holds the idea of a living being, they are not called an awakening hero.

academic_translation: and because, even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, they are not to be called a bodhisattva.
translation: If they hold an idea of a person, they are not called an awakening hero.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever called 'having correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle'.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, there is no thing at all called 'truly entering the awakening hero's vehicle'.

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?
translation: Do you think the Thus-Gone One got any thing from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara to become fully awake to the highest, complete awakening?

academic_translation: When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
translation: After he said this, the honored Subhuti replied to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
translation: Blessed One, the Thus-Gone One did not get any thing at all from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara to become fully awake to the highest, complete awakening.

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: After he said this, the Blessed One spoke to honored Subhuti.

academic_translation: Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
translation: "Subhuti, it is so. It is just so.

academic_translation: There is no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
translation: There is no thing at all by which the Thus-Gone One became fully awake to the highest, complete awakening from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara.

academic_translation: Subhūti, if there were some phenomenon by which the Tathāgata fully awakened, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have prophesied to me, "Young Brahmin, in a future time you will become the Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
translation: Subhuti, if there were some thing by which the Thus-Gone One became fully awake, the Thus-Gone One Dipankara would not have foretold this to me: 'Brahmin boy, in the future you will become the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha named Shakyamuni.'

academic_translation: Subhūti, since there is no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening,
translation: Subhuti, because there is no thing at all by which the Thus-Gone One became fully awake to the highest, complete awakening,

academic_translation: therefore the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, "Young Brahmin, in a future time you will become the Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
translation: That is why the Thus-Gone One Dipankara foretold this to me: "Brahmin boy, in the future you will become the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha named Shakyamuni."

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, because the term "Tathāgata" is a designation for true suchness.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, because 'Thus-Gone One' is a name for the true way things are.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, if anyone were to speak thus: 'The Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening,' they would be speaking falsely.
translation: Also, Subhuti, if someone said, 'The Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha is fully awake to the highest, complete awakening,' they would be speaking falsely.

academic_translation: The Tathāgata calls that one "a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva".
translation: The Thus-Gone One calls that one 'an awakening hero, an awakening hero.'

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata fully awakened to as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, because there is no thing at all that the Thus-Gone One is fully awake to as the highest, complete awakening.

academic_translation: Subhūti, in the phenomenon that the Tathāgata fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.
translation: Subhuti, in the thing that the Thus-Gone One is fully awake to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.

academic_translation: Therefore, the Tathāgata has declared, "All phenomena are the qualities of a Buddha."
translation: Therefore, the Thus-Gone One has said, 'All things are the qualities of a Buddha.'

academic_translation: Subhūti, as for what are called 'all phenomena,' they are all non-phenomena;
translation: Subhuti, what are called "all things" are all non-things.
